title: Uniform tensor-section bound on blowup thickenings
statement:
Let $R_0$ be a Noetherian commutative ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and $K_0\subseteq R_0$ an ideal. There exist integers $d\geq1$ and $q\geq0$, depending only on the degree-preserving unital ring isomorphism class of $\operatorname{gr}_{K_0}(R_0)$ [def-weil-pbc-associated-graded-ring], with the following property for every Noetherian commutative ring $R$ and ideal $K\subseteq R$ with a degree-preserving unital ring isomorphism $\operatorname{gr}_K(R)\cong\operatorname{gr}_{K_0}(R_0)$. Let $b:X=\operatorname{Bl}_K(\operatorname{Spec}R)\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ be the affine blowup [def-nagata-affine-blowup]. Its extended ideal $\mathcal J=K\mathcal O_X$ is invertible [def-sc-invertible-module]. For $n\geq1$ put $Y_n=V(\mathcal J^n)$, $A_n=R/K^n$, $\mathcal L_n=\mathcal J|_{Y_n}$, and let $b_n:Y_n\to\operatorname{Spec}A_n$ be the induced morphism. The ideal inclusion induces $s_n:\mathcal L_n\to\mathcal O_{Y_n}$. For a module sheaf $\mathcal F$, write $\mathcal F(r)=\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal L_n^{\otimes r}$ for $r\geq0$, with tensor product as in [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]; for $r\geq e\geq0$ let $\delta_e:\mathcal F(r)\to\mathcal F(r-e)$ be induced by $s_n^{\otimes e}$. Global sections mean sections on the whole Zariski space $Y_n$. For every $r\geq q$, the canonical multiplication map
$$\theta_{n,r}:K^r/K^{n+r}\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(Y_n,\mathcal L_n^{\otimes r})$$
is an isomorphism. These maps commute with $\delta_e$ (where $r-e\geq q$) and with multiplication by elements of $K^e$: respectively the quotient maps on ideal representatives and the products of representatives. Let $n\geq c\geq0$ with $n\geq1$, and let $N$ be a finite $A_n$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] such that each $a\in K^c$ acts on $N$ through a finite free $A_n$-module. Put $P_n(N)=b_n^*\widetilde N$ using [def-pc-module-pullback], where $\widetilde N$ is the associated quasi-coherent module on $\operatorname{Spec}A_n$ [pqf-def-coherent]. For $v\geq0$ let
$$\eta_{N,v}:K^v\otimes_R N\longrightarrow\Gamma(Y_n,P_n(N)(v))$$
send $x\otimes z$ to the product of the section of $\mathcal L_n^{\otimes v}$ induced by $x\in K^v$ and the pulled-back section $z$. The tensor product of modules is that of [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. If $r\geq q+(d-1)c$, then
$$\operatorname{im}\bigl(\Gamma(\delta_{(d-1)c}):\Gamma(Y_n,P_n(N)(r))\to\Gamma(Y_n,P_n(N)(r-(d-1)c))\bigr)\subseteq\operatorname{im}(\eta_{N,r-(d-1)c}).$$
No completeness assumption on $R$ is imposed.

source.place: Tags 0GA6 (section-uniform), 0GA7 (lemma-bound-q-and-d), parts (1)-(2), and 0GAA (lemma-vanishing-coh-almost-projective), parts (4)-(5), with tensor products replacing the erroneous ideal-product notation; d is enlarged to max(1, the actual fibre dimension).

proof.text: Set $S=\operatorname{gr}_{K_0}(R_0)$ and choose the invariant $d\geq1$ of [lem-per-blowup-graded-cohomological-bound]. For each allowed $(R,K)$ it gives that every $Y_n$ is Noetherian and coherent cohomology on $Y_n$ vanishes above $d$. By [thm-nagata-blowup-principalizes-center], $\mathcal J$ is an invertible ideal locally generated by a non-zero-divisor. On a standard blowup chart with exceptional generator $a$, the degree-one basis of $\mathcal O_X(1)$ maps to $a\in\mathcal J$; the change from $a$ to $b$ multiplies both bases by $a/b$. The canonical chart multiplication of [lem-sfb-standard-proj-twist-tensor] therefore gives $\mathcal O_X(1)=\mathcal J$, compatibly with its inclusion. The Rees algebra modulo its coefficient ideal $K$ has degree $r$ equal to $K^r/K^{r+1}$. Hence [lemma-nagata-relative-proj-base-change-arbitrary] identifies $Y_1$ with $\operatorname{Proj}(S)$, and [lem-sfb-graded-proj-quotient-twist-comparison] identifies $\mathcal L_1$ with $\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Proj}S}(1)$, preserving canonical sections. All these descriptions are invariant under the specified graded ring isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0GA6, first four paragraphs, with the explicit positive twist convention

proof.text: The ring $S_0=R_0/K_0$ is Noetherian: lift an ideal to $R_0$ and reduce a finite generating family. Finitely many generators of $K_0$ map to degree-one algebra generators of $S$. If $\operatorname{Proj}S$ is empty, [lem-sfb-finite-graded-module-section-tail], applied to the graded module $S$, gives $S_r=0$ for all sufficiently large $r$, and higher cohomology is zero. Otherwise choose a finite nonempty degree-one generating family and the resulting graded surjection $S_0[T_0,\ldots,T_m]\twoheadrightarrow S$. By [lem-sfb-graded-proj-quotient-twist-comparison] this gives a closed immersion into $\mathbf P^m_{S_0}$ with the indicated twists. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-serre-vanishing] to its structure sheaf (Noetherian by [lem-sfb-standard-proj-coherent-section-finiteness], hence its finite free rank-one structure module is coherent by [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth]). Together with [lem-sfb-finite-graded-module-section-tail], choose $q\geq0$ so that $S_r\to H^0(Y_1,\mathcal L_1^{\otimes r})$ is an isomorphism and $H^i(Y_1,\mathcal L_1^{\otimes r})=0$ for all $i>0,r\geq q$. Choose this $q$ for the fixed representative $S$; transporting along a graded ring isomorphism gives the same assertions for every allowed pair.

source.place: Tag 0GA6, paragraph defining q(S); coherent.tex Tags 0AG6 and 0AG7

proof.text:
We prove simultaneously for every $r\geq q$ that $H^{>0}(Y_n,\mathcal L_n^{\otimes r})=0$ and that the canonical map $\theta_{n,r}$ is an isomorphism, by induction on $n\geq1$. Step 2 is the base. In the induction step work on $Y_{n+1}$, extending sheaves on its closed subschemes by zero. Multiplication identifies the kernel of $\mathcal O_{Y_{n+1}}\to\mathcal O_{Y_1}$ with $\mathcal J/\mathcal J^{n+1}\cong\mathcal J\otimes(\mathcal O_X/\mathcal J^n)$. This is checked in the local free basis $a$ of $\mathcal J$: $a\otimes\bar x\mapsto ax$, whose kernel is zero since $a$ is a non-zero-divisor. Tensoring with the invertible $\mathcal J^{\otimes r}$ is exact because locally it is tensoring with a free rank-one module. Consequently
$$0\longrightarrow\mathcal L_n^{\otimes(r+1)}\longrightarrow\mathcal L_{n+1}^{\otimes r}\longrightarrow\mathcal L_1^{\otimes r}\longrightarrow0$$
is exact (with the closed pushforwards understood). Closed pushforward preserves the cohomology and coherence by [lem-pc-closed-immersion-coherent-cohomology].

source.place: Tag 0GA7 (lemma-bound-q-and-d), induction on n, displayed short exact sequence

proof.text:
Apply the long exact cohomology sequence [pqf-def-cohomology] to Step 3. At every positive degree the outer groups vanish by the inductive hypothesis at $r+1$ and the base case at $r$, so the middle group vanishes. At degree zero, $H^1(Y_n,\mathcal L_n^{\otimes(r+1)})=0$ makes the bottom row short exact. Compare it with
$$0\to K^{r+1}/K^{r+n+1}\to K^r/K^{r+n+1}\to K^r/K^{r+1}\to0.$$
The canonical multiplication maps give a commutative diagram because both inclusions and restrictions send a representative to that same representative. The left and right vertical maps are isomorphisms by induction and the base case. Explicitly, to lift a bottom middle element, lift its right image using the top row, subtract, and lift the remaining left element; an element in the kernel has zero right image and then zero left representative. Thus the middle map is an isomorphism. This proves the simultaneous induction without completing $R$.

source.place: Tag 0GA7, proof of parts (1)-(2), exact-row comparison

proof.text: For $x\in K^r$, on a chart where $\mathcal J=(a)$ the section defining $\theta_{n,r}$ has coefficient $x/a^r$ in the free basis $a^r$. The morphism $\delta_e$ sends it to $a^e(x/a^r)$ in the basis $a^{r-e}$, which is the section induced by the same ideal representative $x$, now in $K^{r-e}$. For $y\in K^e$, multiplying the section of $x$ by that of $y$ gives coefficient $(x/a^r)(y/a^e)=xy/a^{r+e}$. Thus the quotient and product compatibilities hold on every chart and glue; no cancellation on $Y_n$ is used. The same formulas show that $\eta_{N,v}$ is $R$-balanced, hence defines the asserted map from $K^v\otimes_R N$, by the universal property of [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product].

source.place: Tags 0GA6-0GA7, canonical ideal-representative maps; explicit chart verification

proof.text: Fix $n,c,N$ as in the statement, and put $A=A_n$. This ring is Noetherian by the quotient-ideal argument of Step 2. Choose a finite free surjection $p:A^t\twoheadrightarrow N$, with kernel $M$ finite by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite]. For $a\in K^c$, factor $\bar a\operatorname{id}_N$ through a finite free module and lift the second map through $p$ by lifting its finitely many basis elements. This gives $h_a:N\to A^t$ with $p h_a=\bar a\operatorname{id}_N$. If $i:M\hookrightarrow A^t$, then $\bar a\operatorname{id}_{A^t}-h_ap$ has image in $i(M)$, defining $t_a:A^t\to M$ with $it_a=\bar a\operatorname{id}_{A^t}-h_ap$. Restriction gives $t_ai=\bar a\operatorname{id}_M$. Thus $M$ has the same finite-free scalar-factorization property, proved directly rather than assuming flat pullback.

source.place: Tag 0GAA, first paragraph, and more-algebra.tex Tag 0G95; explicit syzygy lifting

proof.text:
Write $P(T)=b_n^*\widetilde T$. Using [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections] at the unit basic open, [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-affine-sections] identifies the pullback maps on every affine chart with the original maps tensored with its coordinate ring. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-right-exact] gives $P(M)\to\mathcal O_{Y_n}^t\to P(N)\to0$ exact. These pullbacks are quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-quasi-coherent], and finite type because a finite generating family pulls back to a local generating family. They are coherent by [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth]. Let $\mathcal B$ be the kernel of the first map and $\mathcal G$ its image. Kernels, cokernels and finite sums of coherent sheaves are coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-modules-kernel-cokernel-sum], so
$$0\to\mathcal B\to P(M)\to\mathcal G\to0,\qquad 0\to\mathcal G\to\mathcal O_{Y_n}^t\to P(N)\to0$$
are short exact sequences of coherent sheaves. Pulling back $t_ai=\bar a\operatorname{id}_M$ shows that $\bar a$ kills $\mathcal B$. Since these $a$ generate $(K^c/K^n)\mathcal O_{Y_n}=\operatorname{im}(s_n^{\otimes c})$, the map $\delta_c:\mathcal B(v)\to\mathcal B(v-c)$ is zero whenever $v\geq c$: in a local basis it is multiplication by the local generator of that ideal.

source.place: Tags 0GA8 and 0GAA, pullback defect and the two short exact sequences

proof.text: All hypotheses of [lem-per-near-projective-higher-cohomology-loss] now hold on $Z=Y_n$: use $A=R/K^n$, $I=K/K^n$, $g=b_n$, $\mathcal L=\mathcal L_n$, $s=s_n$, the coherent cohomological bound from Step 1, and the acyclicity of the line twists from Step 4. The image of $I^c$ is $K^c/K^n$ for $c\leq n$; the factorizations of Steps 6 apply to each element. In particular, if $d=1$ then $H^1(P(M)(v))=0$ for $v\geq q$; if $d\geq2$ then the decreasing-twist map on $H^1(P(M))$ with loss $(d-2)c$ is zero for $v\geq q+(d-2)c$ (when $d=2$ this means the whole $H^1$ group is zero).

source.place: Tag 0GAA, positive-degree estimates (1)-(3) used in the proof of (4)-(5)

proof.text: Suppose first $d=1$ and $r\geq q$. The first short exact sequence of Step 7 gives $H^1(P(M)(r))\to H^1(\mathcal G(r))\to H^2(\mathcal B(r))$. The first term is zero by Step 8 and the last by Step 1. Thus $H^1(\mathcal G(r))=0$, and the second sequence makes $\Gamma(\mathcal L_n^{\otimes r})^t\to\Gamma(P(N)(r))$ surjective. Here we use the long exact sequence [pqf-def-cohomology]. Finite sums commute with cohomology since an additive derived functor preserves finite biproducts. The required twist loss is $(d-1)c=0$.

source.place: Tag 0GAA, proof of (4), with d enlarged to at least one

proof.text: Suppose $d\geq2$, and set $v=r-(d-1)c\geq q$. Given $\sigma\in\Gamma(P(N)(r))$, let $\xi\in H^1(\mathcal G(r))$ be its boundary under the second sequence of Step 7. In the first sequence its next image lies in $H^2(\mathcal B(r))$. The map $\delta_c$ on this latter group is zero because the sheaf map is zero. Naturality of boundaries [lem-sfb-module-cohomology-fmap-boundary], applied over the identity of $Y_n$, therefore implies that the image of $\xi$ in $H^1(\mathcal G(r-c))$ lifts to some $\zeta\in H^1(P(M)(r-c))$. Now $r-c\geq q+(d-2)c$. Step 8 kills the image of $\zeta$ after the additional loss $(d-2)c$. Commutativity with $P(M)\to\mathcal G$ makes the image of $\xi$ in $H^1(\mathcal G(v))$ zero. Naturality of the other boundary then shows that $\delta_{(d-1)c}\sigma$ has zero boundary and hence lifts to $\Gamma(\mathcal L_n^{\otimes v})^t$ by exactness [pqf-def-cohomology]. This argument also covers $c=0$: the defect sheaf is zero, so the first lift needs no twist loss.

source.place: Tag 0GAA, proof of (5), with the omitted boundary argument made explicit

proof.text: In both cases the required section is the image of a tuple in $\Gamma(\mathcal L_n^{\otimes v})^t$, where $v=r-(d-1)c$. By Step 4 represent its entries by $x_1,\ldots,x_t\in K^v$. Put $z_j=p(e_j)\in N$. The image tuple is exactly $\eta_{N,v}(\sum_j x_j\otimes z_j)$: on a chart with generator $a$, both expressions are $\sum_j (x_j/a^v)(1\otimes z_j)$ in the basis $a^v$. Therefore it lies in $\operatorname{im}\eta_{N,v}$, proving the stated inclusion. For $N=0$, for $K=R$ (all $Y_n$ empty), and for nilpotent $K$ (the blowup is empty), the same proof gives zero targets. Throughout the only constants chosen were $d$ and $q$ from the fixed graded ring; completeness was never used.

split_report.summary: Eleven-step split of the corrected tensor formulation. Proves uniform acyclicity and ideal-quotient sections by induction on the exceptional thickening, checks both map compatibilities on charts, constructs the near-projective syzygy and killed pullback defect directly, and kills the section boundary using a positive-degree estimate. Two new statement-only supporting lemmas; all Serre, Proj, tensor, coherence and boundary tools reused. No statement change. The source direction typo and empty-exceptional-divisor error are documented in report.md.
